text: Open with the business point, not the technology. Say: this is not a proposal to do random AI experiments. It is a strategy to convert our technical textile know-how, quality evidence, and process data into measurable advantage. The deck recommends one low-risk pilot first, then a staged platform only after value is proven.

text:

- Name one executive sponsor and one owner each from R&D, production, quality, packaging, IT, and finance.

text: Make the ask concrete. Management should not feel they are approving a vague transformation program. They are approving a limited 12-week pilot with a bounded budget, no machine control, and clear owners. Emphasize that the pilot is designed to discover measurable value before any larger platform decision.

text: This is the main recommendation. Say that the pilot is deliberately narrow. It is not an AI platform, not a machine-control project, and not a computer vision science project. It is a practical read-only quality intelligence pilot. It should make repeated defects visible and show whether our data can support prediction.

text: This architecture lowers fear. Read-only means we observe and learn first. The output is a roll-level passport and dashboard. Later we can add predictive quality and process recommendations, but only after we trust the data and people trust the system.

text: Avoid fake precision. Say that we should not invent savings before seeing internal baselines. The pilot's job is to calculate the real value pool. The financial equation is simple: scrap, rework, root-cause time, release time, and complaints.
